newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica shoots up in frenetic trade.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica shoots up in frenetic trade.

text.p: Shares in Telefonica de Espana jumped higher in frenetic trade on Friday ahead of Wall Street's opening following its announcement of a global alliance with BT and MCI.
"We're just seeing some speculative activity," said one trader. "It's probably U.S. investors taking positions ahead of Wall Street's open."
Traders said people could also be taking positions ahead of an analysts' briefing on the alliance at 4.00pm (1400 GMT).
By 1330 GMT, shares were up 35 pesetas, or 1.12 percent, at 3,600, with nearly six million shares traded.
The Ibex-35 index of leading shares was largely flat, rising just 0.06 percent, to 5,631.20.
Typically, Telefonica trades some three to five million shares a day.
Analysts said although the partnership had been widely expected, it had been received well by the market.
"Foreign investors have viewed the alliance very positively and there has been quite a lot of buying interest," said Nick Smith, a dealer at BZW in Madrid.
He added that the share offered good value up to 3,900 pesetas, according to BZW's valuation.
The shares slipped 10 pesetas at the opening, after British Telecommunications announced that Telefonica would join its Concert alliance.
But traders said the deal, which involves BT buying two percent of Telefonica over the next 12 months, augured well for the share price on a broader time horizon.
